posts.text: Bottom line: The president should not be able to own and trade stocks. Or the vice president. Or members of Congress.

Then: President Jimmy Carter sold his peanut farm to a blind trust to avoid even the slightest appearance of corruption.

Now: Trump traded over 3,700 stocks earlier this year—personally profiting off of companies who are directly impacted by his decisions as President.
This is common sense: Congress should prevent the President and his family from profiting off crypto deals while in office.

This level of corruption is truly staggering.

As Donald Trump gives corporate monopolies a free pass to screw over people with higher prices, I'm glad that states like California are fighting back.

Much-needed anti-monopoly leadership from Governor @GavinNewsom.


Bloomberg Government (@BGOV)

A major expansion of California’s antitrust laws advanced in the state legislature Thursday as Gov. Gavin Newsom also proposed ramping up funding to crack down on anticompetitive business practices. news.bgov.com/bloomberg-gove…

A majority of Americans can’t afford rent on a modest 2 bedroom.

People aren't buying their first home until 40.

Since 1990, the cost of housing is up 174% while wages have flatlined.

We're in a housing crisis. Congress needs to act like it.

Trump sued his own government to pay himself $10 billion in taxpayer funds.

He even said: "It's awfully strange to make a decision where I'm paying myself."

It's not strange. It's corrupt.

I don't say this often, but Fox News got this exactly right on Trump’s ballroom.

$15M for painting the Lincoln Reflecting Pool electric-blue.

$100M for a giant Arch named after Trump.

$1B for Trump’s ballroom.

If this administration is interested in rooting out government waste, they can take a look at Trump's taxpayer-funded vanity projects.

This is corruption on steroids.

abcnews.com/US/trump-poised-…

Millions of Americans use buy-now-pay-later because they're stretched thin.

The last thing they need is to be penalized on their credit score for it—especially with no transparency, no consistency, and no recourse.

I’m demanding answers.

Defeating Trump just to go back to business-as-usual won't be enough. We need to hold him and his cronies accountable for breaking the law.

Then we need to clean up the corruption in Washington to guarantee our government can never be hijacked again.

That’s what I’m focused on.

Our government isn’t broken.

It works great for billionaires.

For Big Pharma.

For Wall Street.

For corporations that can hire lobbyists.

It's rigged for the wealthy and well-connected.

We need to build a better system—one that works for working people.

Donald Trump is the most corrupt president of all time.


FactPost (@factpostnews)

Last quarter Trump purchased millions in stock for 15 companies.

All 15 of their CEOs were invited to accompany him on his official China visit:
